elements.label: Table 2.2
elements.title: How standards may reduce transaction costs and address market failures
elements.content:
ROLE OF STANDARDS | PURPOSE | TYPE OF STANDARD USUALLY APPLICABLE (VOLUNTARY OR MANDATORY) | MAIN FUNCTION | OUTCOMES
Diffusing information | Offer codified good practices | Mostly voluntary | Quality | • Knowledge transfer
• Quality upgrading
• Productivity
Addressing coordination failures | Provide common specifications | Voluntary and mandatory | Compatibility, measurement | • Economies of scale
• Compatibility
• Lower transaction costs
• Variety reduction
Promoting competition | Provide common specifications | Voluntary and mandatory | Quality, compatibility | • Lower switching costs
• Transparent information
• Competition
Reducing information asymmetries | Provide transparent, reliable, or consistent information | Mostly mandatory | Quality, compatibility, measurement | • Lower search and transaction costs
• Higher trust and consumer protection
Addressing negative externalities | Define thresholds, processes, or technologies to reduce harm to others | Mostly mandatory | Quality | • Environmental protection
• Social sustainability
• Economic fairness
Source: WDR 2025 team.
Note: Whereas this table illustrates typical patterns, real-world standards often serve multiple purposes simultaneously, for instance, blending measurement, compatibility, and quality functions.
